title: Add RBACv2 policy packager, CMK attribution, and audit deduper
author: Asha Kumar
release_notes: Adds a stable RBACv2 policy packager CLI for compiling role templates with residency labels; introduces per-request CMK attribution headers for clearer KMS billing and audit; deploys an audit-ingest deduper to reduce duplicate audit noise in high-throughput environments. Backwards compatible; opt-in via feature flag.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces three coordinated pieces to improve compliance operations and reduce audit noise: (1) rbac-packager: a CLI and library that composes RBACv2 policy templates with tenant/geo labels and outputs a validated bundle for staging and canary rollouts; (2) cmk-attributor: middleware that attaches deterministic CMK attribution metadata to KMS usage events so audit records can tie CMK use to tenant-level contracts; and (3) audit-deduper: an ingest pipeline stage that coalesces identical audit events within a short time window to avoid alert and storage storms from retries and high-frequency service calls.
Motivation: customers operating across multiple jurisdictions requested clearer policy bundles for compliance reviews, more precise KMS usage attribution for billing and key-residency proofs, and lower audit noise to make incident signals actionable.
How it works:
- rbac-packager: takes role templates (templates/roles/*.yaml), tenant claims, and a residency map, validates constraints (no cross-zone elevated grants), and emits a signed bundle (rbac-bundles/<tenant>-v<N>.json) plus a compact manifest used by the policy deployer. Packaging performs static checks (mutually exclusive grants, temporal bounds) and produces an explainability map for auditors.
- cmk-attributor: small middleware inserted in the kms-proxy path (service/kms/proxy/attributor.go) that: 1) resolves the effective CMK used (explicit or derived), 2) attaches an attribution header X-Redwood-CMK-Attribution: tenant=<id>;bundle=<bundle-id>;hash=<short-hash>, and 3) emits a trace/span with cmk.attribution=true. The header is HMAC-signed with the service key so downstream audit processors can validate provenance.
- audit-deduper: a streaming operator in audit-ingest that groups events by (principal, action, resource, cmk-attribution, event-type) and coalesces events when they are bitwise-equal in payload within a 4s sliding window (configurable). Coalesced entries include a count and a first/last timestamp to preserve fidelity while reducing downstream fanout.
Implementation notes and tradeoffs:
- Default dedupe window is conservative (4s) to avoid collapsing unrelated events; operators can tune it per pipeline.
- CMK attribution header intentionally uses a short hash (first 8 bytes of SHA256) to avoid exposing full key IDs in logs while preserving uniqueness for auditing.
- Packager outputs are signed with the org signing key to ensure deployer integrity; signing key rotation is supported via signer plugin.

Review conversation (selected):
- Renee Alvarez (reviewer): "Nice end-to-end design. Two asks before approval: (1) make the dedupe window configurable via an annotation per tenant (we have some APIs with 100ms idempotency), and (2) add a short doc section on how deduping interacts with our evidence retention requirements."
- Asha Kumar (author): "Good catches. Added tenant-level annotation parsing to the deduper operator and expanded docs to clarify retention (deduper preserves full payloads and timestamps—only consolidates identical events and records counts)."
- Michael Chen (reviewer): "Attributor header is useful, but please ensure we don't leak full CMK ARNs in plaintext to logs. Prefer short-hash and sign it."
- Asha Kumar: "Switched to 8-byte SHA256 prefix and HMAC signing; added a verification helper in audit-ingest to validate signatures before coalescing."
- CI-bot: "integration/audit-ingest flaky on first run (timeout in deduper integration test), rerunning..."

Post-review actions and ops notes:
- Feature flag auditDeduper=false on main; rollout via canary: enable for 5% of audit traffic for 72h, check dedupe counts and alert rates.
- Packager is non-blocking: deployer can continue to accept inline policies; packager bundles are consumed only when deployer is set to 'bundle' mode.
- KMS: requires a short window maintenance to reconfigure proxy to add attribution header; ops runbook added to docs/compliance/cmk-attribution.md.
Backwards compatibility and migration:
- No breaking API changes.
- Default behavior unchanged until feature flags enabled.
- Administrators should run packager in dry-run mode to verify bundles before enabling bundle-mode in deployer.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: deploy to staging, enable cmk-attributor in staging kms-proxy, run packager dry-run against sample tenants
- Week 2: enable audit-deduper for 5% production traffic, monitor alerts and retained-events metric
- Week 3: increase to 50% if no regressions, enable bundle-mode for non-critical tenants
- Week 4: GA and add to compliance evidence package
Notes for auditors:
- Packager produces signed bundles and a human-readable explain map suitable for compliance review.
- Audit-deduper preserves payloads and timestamps while annotating coalesced counts; security teams can always opt to disable deduper in specific pipelines if full event duplication is required.
Related: ENG-2765 (policy-packaging spec), SEC-88 (kms-attribution compliance request), SUP-4122 (customer support ticket requesting clearer KMS billing).
